title: A character is built from parts, not from one capsule
note: An enemy is at least five meshes — head, torso, arms, legs — or a modelled asset; one capsule is a placeholder.
intent: One capsule is what a prototype uses to stand in for a person, and it is what the judge sees. Build the figure from at least a head, a torso, two arms and two legs as separate meshes in one group, proportioned from a real height (a head is about an eighth of it), with the shoulders wider than the hips and the limbs tapering. Parent the parts so a simple walk cycle can rotate them from update(dt). When Blender is available, model the character instead and load it with loadAsset — an asset counts as built from parts.

check.js: objects('enemy').length > 0 && objects('enemy').every(o => { if (o.userData && o.userData.asset) return true; let n = 0; o.traverse(c => { if (c.isMesh) n++; }); return n >= 5; })
check.note: Each enemy is at least 5 meshes (head, torso, two arms, two legs…) — a single capsule is a placeholder. A modelled asset (userData.asset from src/assets.js) counts as built from parts.

port: The characters facet builds one makeFigure({ height, seed, palette }) and reuses it for every villager, varying proportions and colour from the seed.
